ti: Sistema de Visión Artificial para la Detección Temprana de Moniliasis en Mazorcas de Cacao
txt: sistema de vision artificial para la deteccion temprana de moniliasis en mazorcas de cacao por extraer pendiente de extraccion a texto completo la moniliasis, causada por el hongo moniliophthora roreri, es la enfermedad mas devastadora del cacao en latinoamerica, responsable de perdidas de hasta el 50 % de la cosecha en colombia. la deteccion temprana es critica para interrumpir el ciclo de esporulacion, pero actualmente depende de la inspeccion visual manual por parte de agricultores con experiencia variable. este proyecto presenta savia (sistema artificial de vision inteligente aplicada), un sistema de vision artificial disenado para la deteccion automatica de las tres etapas de la moniliasis en mazorcas de cacao: joroba (deformacion temprana), mancha cafe (lesion necrotica intermedia) y espora blanca (esporulacion tardia). el sistema implementa una arquitectura jerarquica de dos modulos: un detector de fruto (yolov11s-seg, map50: 93.7 %) que aisla la mazorca mediante enmascaramiento de fondo, y un especialista en patologias (yolov11l-seg) que analiza exclusivamente los pixeles del fruto, eliminando el 100 % del error de entorno (falsos positivos en troncos y ramas) presente en arquitecturas convencionales. se desarrollo una herramienta de etiquetado propia (savia-labeler) basada en el segment anything model para generar poligonos de segmentacion de alta precision. ante un desbalance critico del dataset (76.2 % anotaciones sanas vs. 3.2 % esporas blancas), se diseno un pipeline de manufactura de datos sinteticos que combina deformacion geometrica de malla para jorobas, composicion con poisson blending para manchas, y parchado de texturas reales para esporas. se proyecta que la inyeccion de un 5 % de datos sinteticos por clase eleve el map50 global del especialista de 48.5 % a 55.1 %, con ganancias de hasta 16 puntos porcentuales en la clase de joroba.

ti: Adoption of Innovations for Cacao Pest and Disease Management in Huila, Colombia: Insights From Regression and Social Network Analysis
txt: adoption of innovations for cacao pest and disease management in huila, colombia: insights from regression and social network analysis por extraer pendiente de extraccion a texto completo cacao ( theobroma cacao l.) is fundamental to rural economies in colombia, with huila contributing 8% of the national output. however, its production is severely constrained by pests and diseases, such as moniliophthora roreri , phytophthora palmivora , and carmenta foraseminis , which can cause yield losses of 30%100%. limited adoption of integrated pest and disease management (ipdm) practices among smallholders exacerbates these constraints, undermining sustainability. this study identifies the socioeconomic and institutional factors associated with ipdm adoption in huila. because the data are crosssectional, relationships are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. a survey of 156 cacao farmers across six municipalities (2024) was analyzed using beta and fractional regression models, suitable for proportional outcomes, complemented by cooccurrence and social network analysis. the innovation adoption index (inai), rebuilt to exclude items used as predictors, averaged 0.63, indicating moderate adoption. after controlling for farmer, farm, and institutional characteristics, participation in training (average marginal effect, ame = 0.148; p = 0.024), access to extension services (ame = 0.116; p = 0.004), and credit use (ame = 0.082; p = 0.007) were positively associated with adoption, whereas total farm area was negatively associated (ame = 0.005; p = 0.004). association membership was not individually significant, although the institutional block was jointly significant ( p < 0.001), suggesting an indirect channel operating through training and extension. social network analysis identified extension agents as central knowledge brokers but revealed weak farmertofarmer ties. strengthening cooperative networks, participatory learning, and targeted extension could enhance ipdm diffusion and reinforce sustainable cacao production in colombia.
